title: How do you collect into an unmodifiable result (Collectors.toUnmodifiableList, collectingAndThen + Collections::unmodifiableList), and why does immutability matter for stream outputs?
shortTitle: Collect to unmodifiable result — toUnmodifiableList, collectingAndThen, why immutability matters

s1_definition.profdef: Three ways to collect to unmodifiable: (1) `Collectors.toUnmodifiableList()` (Java 10) — returns unmodifiable list, throws on add/remove/set. (2) `Collectors.collectingAndThen(toList(), Collections::unmodifiableList)` — wraps result after collection. (3) `Stream.toList()` (Java 16) — shortcut, returns unmodifiable list. Immutability matters because stream results are often shared across threads, cached, or returned from APIs — a mutable result can be accidentally modified by the caller, corrupting shared state.

s1_definition.raw:
**Professional definition:** Three ways to collect to unmodifiable: (1) `Collectors.toUnmodifiableList()` (Java 10) — returns unmodifiable list, throws on add/remove/set. (2) `Collectors.collectingAndThen(toList(), Collections::unmodifiableList)` — wraps result after collection. (3) `Stream.toList()` (Java 16) — shortcut, returns unmodifiable list. Immutability matters because stream results are often shared across threads, cached, or returned from APIs — a mutable result can be accidentally modified by the caller, corrupting shared state.

**In simple words (banking analogy):** When the bank gives you a statement (stream result), it should be a SEALED document — you can read it but not alter it. If it's mutable, someone might add fake transactions. Unmodifiable list = sealed statement.

**One line to remember:** toUnmodifiableList() (Java 10), toList() (Java 16) — both unmodifiable. collectingAndThen(toList(), unmodifiableList) for older Java. Immutable outputs = safe sharing.

sections.s2_technical:
Collecting to an unmodifiable result protects shared data from accidental mutation. `Collectors.toUnmodifiableList()`, `toUnmodifiableSet()`, and `toUnmodifiableMap()` (Java 10) return collections that throw `UnsupportedOperationException` on any add/remove/set. This is ideal for returning read-only views of balances or trade lists from a service.

When you must wrap a result of an existing collector, use `collectingAndThen(downstream, finisher)`: `collect(collectingAndThen(toList(), Collections::unmodifiableList))` collects into a list and then wraps it unmodifiable in one expression. Note the difference from `Stream.toList()` (Java 16), which returns an unmodifiable list but allows nulls, whereas `toUnmodifiableList()` rejects nulls.

A banking example: `service.activeAccounts()` returns `accounts.stream().filter(Account::isActive).collect(toUnmodifiableList())`, so callers cannot corrupt the service's internal view. Senior nuance: unmodifiable is shallow — the list cannot be structurally changed, but if it holds mutable objects their fields can still change; prefer immutable element types (records) for true immutability.
sections.s3_banking: Problem — A service returned its internal active-accounts list directly, and a caller accidentally cleared it, corrupting shared state. Fix: collecting with `toUnmodifiableList()` (or `collectingAndThen(toList(), unmodifiableList)`) returns a read-only list that throws on mutation, protecting the service's data.

sections.s5_journey:
**Step 1.** Input: ids [SAV2001, CUR3001, FD4001].

**Step 2.** `filter(id -> !id.startsWith("FD"))` keeps the non-fixed-deposit accounts.

**Step 3.** `toUnmodifiableList()` gathers them into a read-only list.

**Step 4.** Any attempt to `add` or `remove` throws `UnsupportedOperationException`.

**Step 5.** The service can safely hand this list to callers without risk of mutation.

sections.s5b_flow:
```
  ═══ MUTABLE vs UNMODIFIABLE COLLECTORS ═══

  collect(Collectors.toList())           → ArrayList (MUTABLE) — add/remove OK
  collect(Collectors.toUnmodifiableList()) → unmodifiable List — add throws!
  .toList()                               → unmodifiable List — add throws!
  collectingAndThen(toList(), unmod)      → unmodifiable wrapper

  ═══ WHY IMMUTABILITY MATTERS ═══
  Stream result cached in service → caller adds elements → cache corrupted!
  Stream result shared across threads → concurrent modification → bug!
  Unmodifiable result → safe sharing, safe caching, safe API returns.
```

sections.s6_takeaway:
Collect to unmodifiable using toUnmodifiableList (Java 10), Stream.toList() (Java 16), or collectingAndThen wrapping with Collections.unmodifiableList. Immutability matters because stream results are often cached, shared, or returned from APIs — mutable results can be accidentally modified by callers. Note: toUnmodifiableList and toList do NOT allow null elements (throw NPE), while collect(toList()) into ArrayList does. Always prefer unmodifiable results at API boundaries.
